ros_curator.text: The first Johnny was Henri Ollivier, in 1828. He filled a boat with onions, crossed to England and sold the lot. Soon whole crews went each July and came home by Christmas, sleeping in barns and lofts all over Britain.
In Wales they called them Sioni Winwns: Johnny Onions. The trade shrank after the war, but a few Johnnies still cross the Channel each year.
